summary: Latency regression suspected after runtime upgrade (p99 TTFT + p99 end-to-end) on dedicated deployment
environment: prod (us-east; secondary impact observed in eu-west)
related_incident_id: INC-1764271194 (canary-only signature; no public status page event)
description:
Issue summary
- Customer reports a noticeable tail-latency regression after a runtime upgrade on their Dedicated deployment.
- Correlates with internal Q1 baseline sweep signals: a similar p99 TTFT regression signature appeared in perf-canary for long-prefill + mixed chat workloads, but was initially classified as canary-only/no-customer-impact until this report.

Customer impact
- HelioBank reports increased time-to-first-token (TTFT) and overall response time on streaming chat endpoints.
- Impact: degraded UX (customer-facing assistant), increased client-side timeouts, and higher retry volume.
- Customer states this started “within the last ~24 hours” following their scheduled runtime upgrade window.

Timeline (customer-provided)
- 2026-01-18 21:00–23:00 UTC: Dedicated runtime upgrade applied (customer acknowledged maintenance window).
- 2026-01-19 07:30 UTC: First internal alert from customer-side synthetic checks.
- 2026-01-19 15:10 UTC: Customer opens support ticket with request IDs and metrics screenshots.

Environment
- Deployment: Dedicated
- Regions: primary us-east; spillover / DR traffic in eu-west
- Endpoint: /v1/chat/completions (stream=true)
- Runtime build reported by customer: redwood-runtime 2026.01.18.1 (from response headers)
- Previous runtime build (known good): redwood-runtime 2026.01.11.3

Observed symptoms (initial)
- p99 TTFT up ~35–55% on llama-3.1-70b-instruct for peak hours in us-east.
- p95 TTFT up ~15–25%.
- Tokens/sec steady or slightly down (~0–8%), suggesting the regression is dominated by queueing/prefill scheduling and/or kernel selection rather than decode throughput.
- Higher variance than typical; customer notes “spiky” p99.

What we checked (internal)
- Baseline dashboards: p99 TTFT regression for long-prefill cohort in us-east on the same runtime line (matches customer window). Similar but smaller effect in eu-west.
- Scheduler telemetry: increased queue_wait_ms and batch_assembly_ms during the impacted period; batch size distribution shifted toward smaller batches under burst.
- Kernel selection: preliminary suspicion of unintended fallback on one sequence-length regime (requires kernel debug dump to confirm).

Hypotheses
1) Scheduler backpressure thresholds interacting with customer’s traffic shape (bursty tool-calling + occasional long-prefill) causing higher queue wait for chat requests.
2) Kernel auto-selection fallback triggered for certain context lengths, increasing prefill latency and contributing to TTFT.
3) Fleet-level variance: GPU clocking / placement differences post-upgrade (less likely given correlation across canary + customer).

Requested from customer
- 10–20 request IDs spanning before/after (from their client logs).
- Confirmation whether caching mode changed (cold vs warm); customer states “no explicit caching config changes,” but we will validate server-side.

Mitigation plan (proposed)
- Immediate: pin/roll back runtime to 2026.01.11.3 for HelioBank Dedicated cluster if regression confirmed (fastest path).
- Short-term: apply scheduler config override for long-prefill backpressure guardrails if rollback is not possible.
- Follow-up: patch-forward with validated fix once root cause is confirmed, and add this traffic shape to the representative suite gating thresholds.

Dashboards / links (internal)
- Grafana: Perf Baseline / TTFT by cohort (us-east): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/perf-baselines/ttft?var_region=us-east&var_customer=heliobank
- Grafana: Dedicated cluster saturation + queueing: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/dedicated-runtime/queueing?var_cluster=ded-heliobank-us-east
- Looker: Customer latency SLO view (streaming): https://looker.redwood.internal/explore/slo_latency?customer=HelioBank
- Logs (sample): splunk://search?query=customer=HelioBank%20ttft_ms%20model=llama-3.1-70b-instruct%20earliest=-48h

Support ask
- Please confirm whether Redwood can revert/pin the runtime version for HelioBank’s Dedicated cluster and provide an ETA. Customer is requesting mitigation within 24 hours.

2026-01-19 15:36 UTC (Sean Gallagher - SRE): Acknowledged. Seeing matching p99 TTFT bump in us-east on dedicated dashboards; queue_wait_ms is elevated. Pulling per-route breakdown and confirming runtime tag rollout time on their cluster.

2026-01-19 16:05 UTC (Aisha Bello - SRE/Obs): Confirmed SLO view shows p99 degradation for streaming cohort only; non-streaming completion endpoints stable. Suggest focusing on TTFT measurement path + scheduler/prefill overlap changes.

2026-01-19 16:22 UTC (Sofia Ivanova - Runtime Scheduling): The symptom matches the long-prefill backpressure tuning that landed recently. If their traffic mix includes more long-prefill than average, the new defaults could be too aggressive. Recommending temporary override: lower prefill concurrency cap and adjust backpressure thresholds to protect chat TTFT.

2026-01-19 16:41 UTC (Hiro Tanaka - Kernels): Also worth checking kernel fallback. Recent changes add optional dumps for perf runs; for customer cluster we can enable sampled kernel selection debug for 30 minutes to confirm whether we’re falling back on prefill.

2026-01-19 17:10 UTC (Kira Thompson - Support -> Customer): We’re investigating with SRE/runtime. Can you share 10 request IDs (5 before / 5 after) and confirm region(s) impacted? Also confirm whether any client-side streaming behavior changed (buffering/reading cadence).
2026-01-19 18:02 UTC (Customer - HelioBank): Provided 14 request IDs, all us-east. No client changes; same streaming reader. Noted increased timeouts at peak (their 20s client timeout).

2026-01-19 18:24 UTC (Sean Gallagher - SRE): Correlated request IDs to elevated queue_wait_ms spikes. Decode tokens/sec stable. This is consistent with scheduler/backpressure or prefill kernel path rather than general GPU starvation.

2026-01-20 09:15 UTC (Connor O'Brien - Release/Gating): Noted this aligns with perf-canary thread from 2026-01-18 where long-prefill p99 regressed. Suggest rollback for customer now; we can patch-forward after root cause. Logging this for gating exception review.

2026-01-20 10:04 UTC (Sean Gallagher - SRE): Executing mitigation: pin HelioBank us-east dedicated cluster back to redwood-runtime 2026.01.11.3. ETA 30–45 minutes including drain + warmup. Will monitor TTFT p95/p99 and error rate.
2026-01-20 11:02 UTC (Sean Gallagher - SRE): Rollback completed. Early signals: p99 TTFT back within ~5–10% of pre-upgrade baseline. Queue_wait_ms down materially. Monitoring for another peak window.

2026-01-20 11:20 UTC (Kira Thompson - Support -> Customer): We rolled back the runtime in us-east and are seeing TTFT improving. Please confirm whether you see improvement on your side over the next hour.
2026-01-20 12:07 UTC (Customer - HelioBank): Confirmed improvement. Their synthetic checks back to normal. Requesting RCA and guidance on when to safely re-upgrade.

2026-01-21 14:45 UTC (Sofia Ivanova - Runtime Scheduling): Root cause is likely interaction between new backpressure defaults and bursty mixed workload; fix is to adjust defaults and add guardrail for mixed chat + long-prefill. Points to PR: pr-21541 and follow-up config changes. Also recommending we report cold vs warm cache separately in baseline dashboards for this cohort.

2026-01-22 17:30 UTC (Allison Grant - Observability): Added note: ensure TTFT definition is consistent (first-token-on-wire, server-side). Customer measurement includes client network; internal metric is server-side. However, regression magnitude seen server-side is sufficient to explain customer pain. No further action required on definitions for this ticket.

2026-01-24 09:40 UTC (Sean Gallagher - SRE): Patch-forward plan: apply updated scheduler config on newer runtime to HelioBank in staging first; monitor representative suite metrics; then schedule prod upgrade with customer.
2026-01-25 16:12 UTC (Kira Thompson - Support): Customer satisfied with rollback + plan. Leaving ticket in Resolved pending scheduled re-upgrade coordination under separate change request.
resolution: Mitigated customer impact by rolling back/pinning HelioBank Dedicated runtime from 2026.01.18.1 to 2026.01.11.3 in us-east (and keeping eu-west unchanged). Post-rollback monitoring shows p99 TTFT returned near pre-upgrade levels and queueing metrics normalized. Engineering identified likely scheduler/backpressure default interaction with mixed bursty workload; patch-forward will be validated via representative suite + staging before re-upgrade. Customer notified; awaiting scheduled maintenance window for re-upgrade.
